bib.title: Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta
bib.venue: FSE '24 (32nd ACM Symposium on the Foundations of Software Engineering, Porto de Galinhas, Brazil); arXiv:2402.09171v1

question: Can LLM-generated unit tests be made trustworthy enough for industrial deployment by filtering every candidate through build, reliable-pass and coverage-improvement checks before human review?
hypothesis: Embedding LLMs in a pipeline of semantic filters yields only verifiably improving test cases, removing hallucination as a concern, so engineers will accept the output.
contributions: First example of Assured LLM-based Software Engineering (Assured LLMSE) landing LLM code in production with guaranteed improvement.
Evaluation on Instagram Reels and Stories: 75% built, 57% passed reliably, 25% increased coverage.
Report of 2023 development, deployment and evolution at Meta (about 10% of classes improved, 73% of improvements accepted).
Lessons learned, open problems and research challenges.

method.summary: TestGen-LLM prompts two internal Meta LLMs to extend an existing Kotlin test class with extra test cases, then discards every generated test that fails to build, fails any of five executions, or adds no line coverage over existing tests in the same build target. Survivors are submitted as one-test diffs with auto-generated coverage evidence to engineers; evaluated in an offline experiment and three Meta test-a-thons.
method.task: Automated improvement of existing human-written Kotlin (Android) unit test classes; generate-and-test with LLMs

datasets.split: none; dry-run evaluation mode against a fixed baseline

datasets.name: Deployment: Instagram test-a-thons Nov and Dec 2023, Facebook test-a-thon Dec 2023
datasets.size: 1,979 test classes attempted; 196 improved; total trials: Instagram 23,535, Facebook 8,996

inference.decoding: inferred: sampling with temperature; no other decoding detail stated
inference.temperature: default 0.0 after evaluation; deployment tool offered a sweep 0.0 to 1.0 in steps of 0.1
inference.samples: Many trials per test class (a trial = one attempt to generate a test case); number of samples per class not stated; 'LLM ensemble' option combines both LLMs
inference.prompting: Zero-shot single prompt with test class and optionally class under test; four templates (extend_test, extend_coverage, corner_cases, statement_to_complete); default extend_coverage
inference.retrieval: Class under test inserted in prompt (described as RAG-like); no retriever

parameters.coverage_tool: Jacoco line coverage only (branch coverage not available at Meta scale)
parameters.coverage_baseline: all existing test classes sharing the same build target/directory
parameters.dedup_filter: later versions drop previously seen tests by syntactic equality of test bodies
parameters.granularity: per test case (initial MVP was per class)

other.deployment_phases: initial trial of 8 diffs; Nov Instagram test-a-thon (36 engineers, 15-20 Nov 2023); Dec Instagram TestGen-LLM-only (18-20 Dec); Dec Facebook

eval.protocol: Dry-run evaluation mode with a fixed baseline for the 86-class study; deployment results are confounded because coverage accumulates as tests land. No seeds, repeated runs, confidence intervals or significance tests reported.

limits: Both LLMs are undisclosed internal Meta models; no parameter counts, architecture or training data, and tool/code/data not released, so not reproducible.
Line coverage is only a proxy for improvement; branch coverage unavailable at scale and mutation coverage left as future work (Sec 7).

Deployment results confounded: coverage accumulates as tests land, trial counts per setting very unequal (temperature 0 got 30,483 trials), so setting comparisons are weak; no significance tests or repeated runs.
The test-a-thon context (heightened testing focus, authors pre-screening Dec Instagram diffs, engineers pre-warned) may inflate acceptance; Facebook run was out-of-the-box.
Offline study is only 86 classes from two Instagram products; no per-temperature offline table printed.
Filters guarantee no regression and coverage gain, not test quality: diffs were rejected for trivial getters, missing assertions, multi-responsibility tests.
Inconsistent headline numbers: abstract 11.5% improved vs about 10% (196/1,979); 75/57/25 stated as test cases in the abstract and as test classes in Sec 3.3.
Generated tests only append to existing class, so no-regression holds 'by construction'; no comparison to no-filter baseline or to unfiltered LLM output beyond the filter funnel.

terms.definition: embeds the language models, as a service, in a larger software engineering workflow that ultimately recommends fully formed software improvements backed by verifiable guarantees for improvement and non-regression
a test that passes on some occasions and fails on others, when executed in an entirely identical environment; here, one not passing on every one of five executions
